messages:
sam: Quick flag 30fter the migration to the new Docusaurus loader, linkcheck is failing for anchors when a fenced code block immediately precedes a heading. e.g. `#run-example` becomes `run-example-2` and internal links break.
maria: Oof. Do you have a minimal repro? Could be the slugger running twice or a remark plugin ordering issue.
sam: Yep small repro: 
```
```js
console.log('hello')
```

## Run example

Link to it: [run example](#run-example)
```
Linkcheck shows: `WARN anchor mismatch: /docs/run#run-example -> resolved /docs/run#run-example-2`
kevin: Sounds like the heading ID is getting deduplicated because the code block generates an implicit id collision (some parsers add ids for codeblock language?). Less likely but possible. Which remark/rehype plugins are enabled?
sam: We use remark-autolink-headings, rehype-slug, and a custom remark-toc. The site uses the docusaurus default slug function.
maria: Two immediate fixes: 1) add explicit id on the heading `## Run example {#run-example}` if our MD parser supports attr lists; 2) change plugin order so rehype-slug runs after codeblocks are processed. Both are fine but plugin reordering is safer long-term.
kevin: Another option: add a tiny remark plugin that normalizes ids with our canonical slugger (so linkcheck uses same slugging). That prevents double-deduping.
sam: I'll try the explicit id as a quick patch and open a follow-up PR to adjust plugin order and add an integration test.
docs-bot: linkcheck/job/489 started for branch: fix/codefence-heading-anchors  status: running
maria: For the PR note: mention the impact on external links and add a migration snippet in `docs/migration/docusaurus-2.0.md` saying "if you see anchor mismatches, either add explicit heading ids or enable attr_list / adjust plugin order."
sam: Will do. I'll also add a short unit test in `website/tests/linking.test.js` that builds a minimal page and asserts anchor equals expected. Kevin, want to own the follow-up plugin change?
kevin: Yep I can take it after the quick fix PR. We'll also add a CI check in the linkcheck job to fail on deduped anchors (anchor differs from expected) so this doesn't regress.
sam: Great, opening PR now and tagging both of you. Thanks! :rocket:
